nodes.label: Appropriate PostgreSQL data types

nodes.label: Time-range partitioning of large tables

nodes.label: Public Communities
nodes.rationale: Every MVP Community is public, discoverable and owned by exactly one User or Organization. Archiving stops joins and normal discovery while preserving history.

nodes.label: Public and Unlisted Events
nodes.rationale: Events may be hosted by Users, Communities or Organizations. Unlisted events work by direct URL but never appear in discovery. Cancellation remains visibly viewable and blocks new registrations.

nodes.label: Task 149: qualified legal launch review
nodes.rationale: KVKK, 5651, copyright/UGC, child-age, messaging, cross-border processing and conditional EU/GDPR applicability require qualified review. Legal texts, age verification, retention, controller identity and provider deletion terms cannot be approved by code or tests.

nodes.label: Scoped moderation and platform administration
nodes.rationale: Authenticated reporting, resource-scoped moderators and MFA-protected platform admins provide report review, suspension/restoration, resource moderation and verification, with accountable audit references rather than enterprise analytics.

nodes.label: Explicit MVP exclusions
nodes.rationale: No payments/tickets/QR, Guides, AI ranking, premium, private Communities, advanced analytics, enterprise logs, arbitrary organization roles, deep forums, push, custom Socket.IO, microservices, Kafka or Kubernetes; provider chat IDs never replace domain primary keys.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Foundation and local tooling (tasks 1–25)
nodes.rationale: Preserve existing work, configure pnpm/client/server/shared, strict tooling, environment separation, database, API generation, routing, UI/i18n/form/test foundations, Supabase development setup and idempotent discovery seeds.

nodes.label: Phase 2: Public discovery (tasks 26–49)
nodes.rationale: Localized location/category models, public community/event schemas and read APIs, shell/home/details, indexed keyword and combined/date filters, URL-backed discovery, safe host/profile summaries, SEO and browser/API verification.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Accounts and content creation (tasks 50–72)
nodes.rationale: Server JWT identity, signup/login return flow, private/public profiles, signed validated uploads, personal/community-hosted creation, eligible host selection, community edit/archive and event edit/cancel, with creator permission tests.

nodes.label: Phase 4: Participation and capacity (tasks 73–95)
nodes.rationale: Membership/registration state history, idempotent transitions, join/register/leave, My Activity, locked capacity, automatic/manual waitlists and decisions, organizer lists/removal/counts, manual attendance, isolated-PostgreSQL concurrency tests.

nodes.label: Phase 5: Organizations and staff (tasks 96–112)
nodes.rationale: Independent one-owner organizations, public/profile management, organization-owned resources, single-use expiring admin invitations, invitation acceptance, transactional ownership transfer, verification and inherited authority tests.

nodes.label: Phase 6: Discussions and realtime chat (tasks 113–131)
nodes.rationale: Persistent one-level discussions, authorized moderation, stable Stream mappings, server tokens, group eligibility/revocation, isolated React SDK, unified Messages, DMs, bilateral blocking/reporting and outage/access-transition tests.

nodes.label: Phase 7: Notifications, moderation and privacy (tasks 132–149)
nodes.rationale: Durable in-app/email delivery and participation/organization/cancellation wiring, reports and scoped moderators, platform admin MFA and review console, age/legal acceptance, privacy requests/deletion and unresolved counsel gates.

nodes.label: Phase 8: Pre-production and automation (tasks 150–164)
nodes.rationale: E2E, cross-module authorization, security, accessibility, SEO, load/performance, recovery and provider checks precede isolated Render staging, smoke tests and operational checklist; GitHub Actions CI/CD and staging health verification come last without automatic production deployment.

nodes.label: Phase 9: Production and operation (tasks 165–171)
nodes.rationale: After phase 8 passes and owner launch decisions are approved, establish separate production services, secure settings, safely migrate approved data, release a tested build, record go/no-go and assign ongoing operations.

nodes.label: Task 147: age and legal acceptance gate
nodes.norm_label: task 147: age and legal acceptance gate
nodes.rationale: As of 2026-10-28, SupabaseAuthGuard uses PrivacyGateService: new identities are UNVERIFIED and must self-declare 18+ and accept all PUBLISHED document versions. Under-18 identities are refused. Draft empty legal slots remain unpublished pending counsel decisions; code completion is not legal completion.

nodes.label: Task 148: privacy requests and provider cleanup
nodes.norm_label: task 148: privacy requests and provider cleanup
nodes.rationale: ACCESS, EXPORT, DELETION and CORRECTION requests at /privacy have audit trails and 30-day due dates. Exports are JSON; deletion anonymizes Wasl data and waits for retried provider cleanup to SUCCEED or be SKIPPED. Case updates are in-app only, completed deletion has no reachable channel, and retention erasure stays disabled with duration-free TBD_LEGAL rows.

nodes.label: React 19 Vite SPA
nodes.rationale: React Router Data Mode serves the SPA; Next.js and SSR are explicitly excluded, including as an SEO workaround.

nodes.label: Resend and Supabase Queues delivery
nodes.rationale: Server-only Resend adapter with pgmq durable processing, retry and idempotency prevents required transactional notifications from disappearing during provider outages.

nodes.label: Deny-by-default security and reliability
nodes.rationale: Strict boundaries, safe projections/secrets, headers/CORS, throttling, OWASP ASVS/Top 10, revocation tests, safe logs, readiness, graceful shutdown, recovery rehearsal and realistic concurrency/load testing are launch requirements.

nodes.label: Organization verification
nodes.rationale: Pending, Verified and Rejected are platform-controlled states independent of payments or premium; no verification document upload is required for MVP.

nodes.label: WASL
nodes.rationale: Helps Arabs throughout Türkiye discover, evaluate, join and organize Communities and Events, then communicate; the early audience is university students without restricting the nationwide product to them.

nodes.label: docs/PROJECT_HANDOFF.md status source
nodes.rationale: Task checkboxes in this guide are planning markers, not current implementation status; some checked and unchecked entries do not reflect completion timing.

nodes.label: Protected-channel access revocation
nodes.rationale: Only Active members or Accepted attendees and authorized organizers/moderators receive resource chat access. Leaving, removal or role changes revoke provider membership immediately with retries/reconciliation; provider membership is never product authorization.

nodes.label: OpenAPI Orval shared contracts
nodes.rationale: NestJS Swagger generates API schemas and Orval generates Fetch/TanStack Query clients and MSW mocks. Shared TypeScript/Zod contracts contain no database imports; server inputs are revalidated.

nodes.label: Transactional capacity invariants
nodes.rationale: Authoritative capacity counts Active members or Accepted attendees with consistent attendance lifecycle. PostgreSQL locking or conditional transactional updates prevent concurrent overbooking.

nodes.label: Approved design tokens and bilingual accessibility
nodes.norm_label: approved design tokens and bilingual accessibility
nodes.rationale: Owner docs/design assets are the visual source of truth. Semantic Tailwind/shadcn tokens, Tajawal Arabic, Manrope English, i18next and logical CSS support one RTL/LTR layout with keyboard, focus, contrast and reduced-motion behavior.

nodes.label: Persistent lightweight discussions
nodes.rationale: Wasl PostgreSQL stores one Event thread and Community topics with comments and a single reply level, separate from Stream. Read visibility follows the parent; writing and moderation follow resource policy.

nodes.label: NestJS Fastify modular monolith
nodes.rationale: One API with module-owned persistence and business logic; route handlers avoid raw SQL, clients avoid database access, and modules cannot import another module's repositories. Avoid speculative microservices.

nodes.label: Durable dual-channel notifications
nodes.rationale: Persist in-app and email state. Accept/reject, promotion, removal, cancellation, admin invites and verification changes require both channels; cancellation audiences include Accepted, Pending and Waitlisted users.

nodes.label: Organization ownership and inherited authority
nodes.rationale: An Organization survives its creator and has exactly one Owner and zero or more Admins. Transactional transfer cannot orphan or duplicate owners; admins cannot transfer ownership or remove the owner. Owner/Admin authority inherits to hosted resources.

nodes.label: Owner-approved reversible release and operations
nodes.rationale: Tasks 165 and 169–171 require accountable domain/budget/region/legal/performance/recovery decisions, exact staging-tested revision, owner-approved release window and rollback, nondestructive production checks, explicit go/no-go and a named alert/support/recovery owner. Launch sign-off is not delegated.

nodes.label: Membership and registration state transitions
nodes.rationale: Membership states are Pending, Waitlisted, Active, Rejected, Left, Removed. Registrations add Accepted, user cancellation, organizer removal, Attended and No-show. Explicit histories, uniqueness and idempotent actions replace booleans.

nodes.label: Personal identity and contextual authorization
nodes.rationale: Supabase Auth provides identity and server-verified JWTs; NestJS owns product roles and every protected read/command. A human has one personal identity with coexisting resource roles, not an organization shared login.

nodes.label: Production service and data isolation
nodes.rationale: Tasks 166–168 require separate production Supabase/Render and approved email/chat settings, production-only secrets/origins/redirects/storage/admin MFA, no development seeds or credentials, a verified pre-migration backup and twice-confirmed target. Migrations run sequentially.

nodes.label: Public discovery and auth interruption
nodes.rationale: Visitors browse details before signing in; authentication is required when acting and returns users to their original context. Search supports nationwide localized locations, categories and event dates.

nodes.label: Public-only SPA indexing
nodes.rationale: Unhead metadata, canonical/social tags, JSON-LD, sitemap and robots describe public indexable routes. Unlisted, account, chat, management and admin routes must not be indexed; SPA remains approved.

nodes.label: Server and navigation state ownership
nodes.rationale: TanStack Query owns server data; URL parameters own filters/navigation. React state handles local UI, with Zustand only for genuine cross-screen client state.

nodes.label: Stream Chat messaging boundary
nodes.rationale: Stream owns realtime bodies/history; Wasl owns stable user/resource/conversation IDs, mappings and eligibility. SDK imports stay inside backend adapter and frontend Messaging feature; do not mirror full history in PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Vertical-slice delivery
nodes.rationale: Each slice includes schema, API, UI and verification. Public read-only features precede authentication and transactional participation; CI/CD comes last rather than blocking feature delivery.

nodes.label: Policy-specific waitlist promotion
nodes.rationale: Full resources waitlist eligible applicants. Automatic admission promotes oldest eligible users when slots open; manual approval preserves organizer selection and must not be overridden by FIFO. Waitlisted users have no member privileges.

nodes.label: Design sidecar schema version 2
nodes.rationale: The sidecar extends rather than duplicates frontmatter, carrying tonal ramps, motion, shadows, breakpoints, narrative and self-contained shadow-DOM component snippets.

nodes.label: Impeccable Documenter
nodes.rationale: Record reused rules from the shipped artifact after building; never canonize defects or planned rules contradicted by implementation.

nodes.label: Live variant generation fast lane
nodes.rationale: Reuse one existing dev server and browser page, route a named element and direction into live generation, then carbonize the accepted variant and stop only the helper.

nodes.label: Craft floor
nodes.rationale: A shared rendered-result checklist enforces mechanics without choosing art direction; pinned briefs and the committed visual world override habitual defaults.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md normative token frontmatter
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable token values are normative and prose describes application in eight canonical sections; only actual reused implementation tokens belong in scan mode.

nodes.label: Reusable design pattern extraction
nodes.rationale: Extract patterns used at least three times with the same intent, match the existing system and migrate every use; premature abstraction is worse than duplication.

nodes.label: Immediate and Stop detector tiers
nodes.rationale: Interrupt edits only for mechanical immediate issues and defer taste and rhythm findings to a deduplicated session-end deep pass on supporting harnesses.

nodes.label: Development-only CSP allowance consent
nodes.rationale: Detect the CSP patch shape, obtain consent and guard localhost script/connect allowances by development environment; never weaken deployed production CSP for the helper.

nodes.label: Local development setup
nodes.rationale: Requires Node.js 24.19.0 and Corepack pnpm 10.15.1; install then run pnpm dev for web localhost:5173 and API localhost:3000.

nodes.label: Local quality verification commands
nodes.rationale: Documents lint, formatting, typecheck, tests, build, e2e and Storybook builds; new machines must install Playwright Chromium through the web workspace.

nodes.label: Database-free scaffold startup
nodes.rationale: The API can start without a database so health checks work before Supabase setup; migrations and seeds require DATABASE_URL.

nodes.label: Client/server environment secret boundary
nodes.rationale: Commit example templates, not credentials. Client environment may contain only Supabase URL and publishable key; database URL, service-role key, Stream secret and Resend key stay server-side. Vite loads client production environment; local production server uses Node --env-file.

nodes.label: Migration and development seed workflow
nodes.rationale: Generate API and database artifacts, review SQL in server/drizzle before shared-database application, then migrate or seed. Seed provides labeled sample entities and reference data, refuses NODE_ENV=production and must never target production.

nodes.label: Manrope and Tajawal font delivery
nodes.rationale: Preconnect Google Fonts origins, load the stylesheet through print-media switching, and provide a noscript stylesheet fallback.

nodes.label: Wasl provider integrations
nodes.rationale: Supabase provides database, authentication and storage; Stream backs messaging with Wasl-owned eligibility; pgmq queues email delivery through Resend.

nodes.label: Remaining launch approval and verification gaps
nodes.norm_label: remaining launch approval and verification gaps
nodes.rationale: Legal and retention decisions await owner or counsel approval; irreversible retention erasure is disabled, signed-in real-API journeys are not automated, and formatting is not gated by CI.

nodes.label: Wasl bilingual community and event platform
nodes.norm_label: wasl bilingual community and event platform

nodes.label: Graph-first codebase exploration
nodes.rationale: Query the persistent graph before source exploration and update it after code changes; dirty generated graphs are expected.

nodes.label: Server-owned authorization and business rules
nodes.rationale: React remains presentation, NestJS owns domain decisions and database access, and shared packages contain cross-boundary contracts without exposing privileged credentials.

nodes.label: Wasl modular monolith
nodes.rationale: A single NestJS deployable contains data-owning modules with narrow contracts; microservices and extra infrastructure require measured need.

nodes.label: Transactional admission and FIFO waitlists
nodes.rationale: Capacity and waitlist decisions execute inside PostgreSQL transactions to prevent overbooking.

nodes.label: Core Web Vitals
nodes.rationale: Optimization targets LCP below 2.5 seconds, INP below 200 milliseconds and CLS below 0.1.

nodes.label: Carbonize cleanup
nodes.rationale: Bake accepted parameter values into permanent semantic styles and remove preview scaffolding before resuming polling.

nodes.label: Identity lock
nodes.rationale: Record actual palette, typography, topology and component treatment before variation; departure requires an explicit current redesign request.

nodes.label: Live variant editing
nodes.rationale: Local HMR previews preserve identity by default; atomic publication prevents framework reloads from stranding incomplete variants.

nodes.label: Empty-state onboarding
nodes.rationale: Explain what belongs here, why it matters and how to begin; distinguish first use, intentional clearing, no results, no permission and loading failure.

nodes.label: Time-to-value onboarding
nodes.rationale: Onboarding proves value through real actions, optional concise guidance and contextual disclosure rather than exhaustive feature teaching.

nodes.label: Measured interface performance optimization
nodes.rationale: Identify the actual bottleneck, measure before and after, and verify real-device behavior without sacrificing accessibility or functionality.

nodes.label: Contextual technical ambition
nodes.rationale: Enhance how existing features feel, obtain direction approval, retain functional fallbacks, and test smoothness on mid-range devices.

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement
nodes.rationale: New browser capabilities must leave a good usable experience when unsupported; heavy resources initialize near the viewport and pause off-screen.

nodes.label: Critique snapshot backlog
nodes.rationale: Use current fingerprint-matched findings and close only the exact processed snapshot after its Priority Issues are cleared, preserving newer backlogs.

nodes.label: Whole-path polish
nodes.rationale: Refinement preserves identity and behavior, fixes functional and inaccessible paths before cosmetics, and verifies states across viewports and input methods.

nodes.label: Quiet design refinement
nodes.rationale: Reduce noise, saturation, decoration and motion while retaining functional affordances, hierarchy and product personality.

nodes.label: Context-aware command routing
nodes.rationale: Signals and applicable detector findings guide two or three recommendations without automatically executing a selected improvement command.

nodes.label: Typography system refinement
nodes.rationale: Assess typography independently from mechanical findings, preserve established families and role consistency, and verify reading measure, language expansion, scaling and font delivery.

nodes.label: Durable live session journal
nodes.rationale: Append-only session state replays unacknowledged work after restarts rather than requiring the user to repeat actions.

nodes.label: Operate surface mode
nodes.rationale: Working products keep category-standard organization and controls; the visual world contributes type, palette, density and one signature move.

nodes.label: Experience surface mode
nodes.rationale: The work itself leads from the opening viewport; material commitment must still form a usable page rather than a poster.

nodes.label: Persuade surface mode
nodes.rationale: The world may structure the page, but the offer, proof and working primary action must remain intelligible.

nodes.label: Read surface mode
nodes.rationale: A distinctive frame surrounds a calm readable column; familiar document navigation and reading order remain intact.

nodes.label: Code-led build contract
nodes.rationale: Operate and Read default to code-led implementation; compositional ambition remains binding through the written contract and selected sketch.

nodes.label: Comp-led build phases
nodes.rationale: Disk-backed gates enforce comps, spec, plates, hero, sections, motion and responsive fidelity instead of trusting remembered appearance.

nodes.label: Direction contract
nodes.rationale: A development-only surface brief records thesis, visual world, story, first viewport, seed reference and finish obligation; it must never enter browser-delivered artifacts.

nodes.label: Finish review and documentation
nodes.rationale: Fresh-context review uses validated captures and explicit recapture, rebuild, ship or fix dispositions; new visual worlds also require token-bearing design documentation.

nodes.label: Earned familiarity in product UI
nodes.rationale: Stable typography, consistent controls and state-driven motion help tools disappear into the task; overlays must escape clipping ancestors.

nodes.label: Approved-comp region map
nodes.rationale: Name every visible region before asset production; independent content, moving parts and frames need separate composited regions, and comp crops remain reference evidence only.

nodes.label: Confirmed design brief discovery
nodes.rationale: Discover purpose, audience, proof, states and boundaries; resolve direction, confirm a useful brief, and stop before code or contract persistence.

nodes.label: Raster provenance
nodes.rationale: Shipping raster assets carry the exact generation prompt or source origin embedded in the image, alongside their measured region specification.
